# Results — Study 178 (CCI) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — CCI(20) on daily
bars, enter at the next bar's open in the direction of the CCI extreme (oversold/overbought),
exit after a fixed hold window — run across a basket of six liquid instruments and pinned
against a **random-direction control** on the *same* entries. As-of **2026-06-15**. Trades
pooled across the basket: **n = 963** (~160/instrument, ~16/yr/instrument over 10 years).*

## The honest test — breach-entry framing, gross (cost = 0)

A direction-symmetric framing against a random-direction control on identical entries is
the only fair way to ask "does CCI add directional information over a coin?"

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **CCI breach (follow the extreme)** | 963 | **45.1%** | **−33.11** | **−2.06** |
| Random direction (control) | 963 | 50.1% | −4.38 | −0.27 |

- The CCI breach rule's gross expectancy is **−33.11 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **−2.06** —
  **statistically significant, but on the wrong side of zero.** CCI overbought/oversold
  signals forecast the opposite of what the folk rule predicts on these instruments.
- It does **not beat a coin.** Cross − random = **−28.73 bps/trade**; the rule is
  significantly *worse* than picking a random direction.
- The 45.1% win-rate (below 50%) is itself consistent with momentum-dominated markets
  where "oversold" keeps falling and "overbought" keeps rising during the study window.

## Cross-back framing (confirmed bounce), gross (cost = 0), hold=5

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **CCI cross-back** | 963 | **46.3%** | **−28.08** | **−1.68** |
| Random direction | 963 | 46.6% | −26.48 | −1.71 |

The cross-back (confirmed-bounce) framing fares similarly to the breach framing: both arms
are negative, and CCI adds no edge over a coin on these entries.

## Hold-period sweep (breach, gross)

| Hold period | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | 963 | 52.2% | +3.93 | +0.63 |
| 3 days | 963 | 46.7% | −14.18 | −1.10 |
| 5 days | 963 | 45.1% | −33.11 | −2.06 |
| 10 days | 963 | 45.7% | −59.51 | **−2.34** |
| 20 days | 963 | 48.4% | −57.52 | −1.26 |

The 1-day hold is the only positive framing, but its HAC *t* = +0.63 is statistically
indistinguishable from noise. The deterioration at longer windows is consistent with
momentum effects: the instruments that trigger CCI extremes often continue in the direction
of the extreme, not against it.

No instrument shows a positive, statistically significant edge. SPY and QQQ are the most
benign (near-zero), while TSLA drives much of the pooled negative result.

## Cost sweep (breach, hold=5)

At ~16 trades/instrument/year the turnover is low, and costs add little to the pooled
loss — the gross edge is already significantly negative:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −33.11 | −2.06 |
| 0.5 bps | −33.61 | −2.09 |
| 1.0 bps | −34.11 | −2.12 |
| 2.0 bps | −35.11 | −2.18 |

The edge is negative before costs; costs make it worse but are not the primary killer.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same engine recovers a
CCI edge **only when mean-reversion is planted**, and reads ≈ 0 when it isn't:

| Planted AR(1) mean-rev | CCI gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +0.25 (moderate mean-rev) | positive | yes |
| −0.10 (trending) | negative | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Breach gross HAC *t* = −2.06 (wrong sign), 45.1% win-rate, no edge
  over a random-direction control (Δ = −28.73 bps). No instrument shows |*t*| > 1.5 in
  the positive direction.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross expectancy significantly negative → a loser before costs.
  Low turnover (~16 trades/yr) means costs are not the main issue — the signal itself is
  negative.
- **Beats a coin? — BUSTED.** CCI is actively *worse* than a random direction on these
  instruments at this horizon, consistent with momentum dominating mean-reversion.
